title: Best Practices for Reducing Patient No-Shows Tip Sheet - Central California Alliance for Health

facts.fact: The page states that medical practices average a five to 55 percent no-show rate, citing third-party published studies (George & Rubin 2003; Kheirkhah et al. 2016; Fiori et al. 2020).
facts.quote: Medical practices average a five to 55 percent no-show rate, which limits practices in providing efficient care.

facts.fact: The page cites Fiori et al. (2020) on unmet social needs and no-show visits as covering a US Northeastern urban health system during 2018-2019.
facts.quote: Unmet social needs and no-show visits in primary care in a US Northeastern Urban Health System, 2018-2019.

facts.fact: The page recommends blocking time on the calendar each day to allow for walk-in availability and urgent or acute appointments.
facts.quote: Blocking time on the calendar each day allows for walk-in availability and urgent/acute appointments (i.e., ear infection or strep throat).

facts.fact: The page provides a no-show discussion script that emphasizes the importance of attending scheduled appointments and asks patients to call before their appointment time to reschedule or cancel.
facts.quote: it is important for you to attend your appointment. If you need to reschedule or cancel your appointment, please call us at <phone number> before your scheduled appointment time.

facts.fact: The page recommends sending patients an appointment reminder before their visit by phone, email, and/or text.
facts.quote: Send a reminder to your patients before their appointment via phone, email, and/or text.
